text:
Dallas scored five times and the expected goals say the result was, if anything, fair. DAL generated 4.76 expected goals to SJS's 1.57, put up 66 shot attempts to 34, and came out as the deserving winner in 92 percent of simulated replays. The only oddity was how the scoring began: Miro Heiskanen's backhand in the last minute and change of the first period carried just a 3 percent chance of going in, even though DAL had out-chanced SJS 1.74 to 0.22 over those 20 minutes.

The game opened up in the second. Joel Kiviranta scored at 3:17 on a snap shot rated at 63 percent, the best look any DAL goal had, and Jamie Benn made it 3-0 at 6:19. Jason Robertson added the fourth at 16:30, unassisted, finishing a night in which DAL piled up 1.9 expected goals with him on the ice against 0.07 allowed. Mikko Rantanen closed the scoring at 15:22 of the third, with an assist from Sam Steel. All five goals came at even strength, and DAL went 0 for 3 on the power play.

At the other end, Jake Oettinger stopped all 13 shots he faced. That was 1.57 goals better than the chances deserved, though SJS only managed 1.57 expected goals to begin with, so he was rarely asked to rescue anything. Yaroslav Askarov allowed five on 26 shots against 4.76 expected, so he was close to par. SJS did lead in hits (30 to 11) and blocked shots (21 to 13), a sign of a team spending its night without the puck.
